title: The Agent Loop: Observe, Think, Act
service: ReactLoop: a ReAct agent loop over a native-reasoning model, with a tool registry, JSON transcript snapshots, a text front end for prompt-based ReAct models, an SSE stream for the UI and a nested observation formatter

parts.lesson_anchor: The five ingredients (3 stop condition: no tool calls; 5 observation formatter); The 2026 shift: native reasoning (passed through turns); 2026 pitfalls: Loop length explosion; Exercise 2; code/main.py AgentLoop.run and ToolRegistry.dispatch; quiz Q9
planted_bugs: record reads reply['tool_calls'], so a reply that just answers is a KeyError, and run has no 'no tool calls -> done' stop at all
record keeps the readable thinking but drops the opaque reasoning item; the error surfaces one turn later inside ScriptedModel.respond as 'missing reasoning item for assistant turn 1'
dispatch wraps the tool call in except TypeError, so int(None) inside a tool is reported as bad args (the model would keep changing its arguments)
messages() re-renders every past tool result into a new Message on every turn, so the history never holds its observations and a long run is quadratic
parts.timing_assert: 1000 tool turns with 481-496-character results under 0.12 s; the per-turn re-rendering version takes 1.67-1.93 s on this machine (2.8-3.0 s with ten busy processes on ten cores), the fixed loop 8.1-8.8 ms (8.7-16.4 ms under the same load)
parts.overfix_guard: text next to tool calls is not the answer (stop-on-any-text fails); an explicit empty tool_calls list and a reply without text both end the run; finish never reaches the registry; bind_partial and sniffing the TypeError message for 'argument' both fail, and so does a hand-written check that looks only at missing parameters (an extra warehouse argument), only at the argument count (a misnamed item argument) or only at keyword arguments (positional ones, as ReAct text gives them); a cached view that leaves the history without observations, or an observation without its raw result, fails

deviations: Part 1: the reply format is a dict with text, tool_calls, thinking and an opaque reasoning item, and the stand-in provider is strict on purpose: it refuses a conversation whose assistant turn lost or changed its reasoning item, so the missing item surfaces one call away from record. The timing defect is not a prompt rebuilt with string +=: the model reads a message list, so the quadratic work is messages() re-rendering every past tool result into a new Message on every turn. The fix (format each observation once, when the tool returns, and keep it in the history) also makes the transcript show what the model actually read, which Part 2 relies on. Besides the suggested stop-on-any-text guard, the test pins finish as an explicit stop and the raw result next to each observation.

Part 2: messages are saved as dataclasses.asdict fields with reasoning in standard base64, the layout a trace viewer shares. Atomic replacement is checked through a reader that keeps the old file open and a save that fails on a set, not through crash injection, which lesson 34 covers. The tricky tool results are a 61-bit order id, -0.0, 0.1 + 0.2 and a lone surrogate from a note cut in half an emoji; a loaded transcript must also be accepted by a fresh ScriptedModel, so the reasoning bytes have to be exact.

Part 3: arguments are double-quoted strings with JSON escapes, tool names may contain dots (the lesson's kv_store.get), and a step without a readable Action gets one fixed FORMAT_ERROR observation while the reason stays in Step.error. A completion ends at its first Action line as well as at its first Observation line, so text after the action never reaches the scratchpad.

Part 4: stream_run drives the same AgentLoop through the stand-in's stream(), which yields thinking pieces before the reply. Assistant text that comes with tool calls is kept in the history but not streamed, so final is the answer only. The run ends once through finish and once through a turn without tool calls, and the timing probe uses the stand-in's sent counter and the number of tools run.

Part 5: a string result is the observation as it is (only strings inside a structure are JSON-quoted), the budget is cut so that the result with its marker is exactly budget characters, and [cycle] versus {…} is never tested where both would apply.
